e: Burundi agrees to accept third country deportees from the United States, who have not been accused of crimes or having terrorist links.
Eight people are killed and nine others injured in a crowd crush at the Senior Technical School of Kamenge in Bujumbura after a wall at an exit gate collapses.
At least 13 people are killed and 57 are injured after explosions at a military ammunition depot in Bujumbura, reportedly caused by an electrical short circuit.

Former prime minister Alain-Guillaume Bunyoni, who had been sentenced to life imprisonment in 2023 for conspiring against president Ndayishimiye, is granted provisional release from a hospital in Gitega on medical grounds.
Italian authorities arrest Burundian national Guillaume Harushimana in Parma, in connection with the 2014 murders of three Italian missionary nuns in Bujumbura.
The Kavimvira border crossing between the DRC and Burundi reopens following a two-month closure caused by M23 offensives.
At least 25 Congolese refugees are reported to have died in a cholera outbreak in Burundi.
A major national scandal is exposed involving billions of francs in misappropriated fertilizer funds.
A 70-year-old man is murdered in Bubanza.
Eight people are accused of spying for the M23 rebels in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Japan sends $625,000 of food aid to Burundi.
